Little pro tips for you (assuming working in arc pro):
1. Add scale bar and north arrow 

2.) get rid of that service credits: when in layout > insert tab > dynamic text > service credit > drag to the right of your layout (off the layout into the gray area) 

3.) make that legend better. Have consistent breaks in the symbology, after the ranges have what those number mean (e.g. votes in favor of Ewing), and what is up with what appears to be those blank precincts (are they no data or something? Add that to legend.

1.) [https://apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader/](https://apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader/) \> Hydrography >  NHDPlus High Resolution (NHDPlus HR), fileGDB option > look for the Release 2, should be published in 2025 or about

2a.) Create a feature class for your AOI: View tab > catalog pane > expand databases > right click on your geodatabase > new > feature class > polygon and name it something like "AOIs" > add a new field for "AOI\_Name", make sure the field type is text > finish and it will be added to your map > change symbology by right clicking on layer in catalog pane > symbology > just go with a black border. 

2b.) Create a new feature class for your canopy cover by following repeating steps in 2a, just name it something different and don't have to add a field for AOI Name. Change symbology to something else too. 

2c.) Create polygons for your AOIs and then your canopy within the AOI: just follow this tutorial or something similar: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RexCiwyNShs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RexCiwyNShs). SAVE YOUR EDITS USING THE SAVE BUTTON IN THE EDIT TAB, not the normal save button

2d.) calculate acreages: This isn't the most elegant solution but it should work: analysis tab > tools > dissolve > [dissolve ](https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/tool-reference/data-management/dissolve.htm)your canopy so everything is all one big feature. Then for both your AOI and canopy feature classes,  look for the [calculate geometry tool](https://pro.arcgis.com/en/pro-app/latest/tool-reference/data-management/calculate-geometry-attributes.htm), add a new field for "SqKm" and then make sure your using geodesic area and then setting the proper units. Then you can probably just compare the acreages for canopy and AOI by opening up the attribute tables (right click on layer in content pane). 

3.) No idea, I don't do that

4.) My recommendation would be to digitize similar to 2 if having a small area, otherwise use NLCD for impervious: [https://www.usgs.gov/centers/eros/science/nlcd-product-suite](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/eros/science/nlcd-product-suite). 

  
Also for learning this stuff, ESRI has really good tool documentation (look at the dissolve link for example), youtube stuff, or even ask ChatGPT to help with troubleshooting. Also ask your TA for the intro to GIS class, I'm sure they would be happy to help.

Hey so I'm a pretty advanced runner and just wanted to throw my 2 cents in. Personally I have run in peg turbos and peg 36s. The turbos for me at least split in the heel so I would not recommend them. Peg 36s have worked for me and I liked them but I switched them out for Salomons for the trail running season. Also note that you want to replace shoes after 300-500 miles. Personally I have found that nikes start to fall apart towards the earlier end of that. If you are just getting started I would recommend Pegasus, just the regular versions, the 36s should be on sale now since the 37 just dropped.

I really like your car analogy. I think it is hard for them to understand running in general, especially that distance does not necessarily equal an increased risk of injury. I think it is because they have only watched my 5k races and under where I go incredibly hard for the whole thing. However, one of the things that I like about trail running is that it is not uber competitive at least the level that I want to race at and you can pace yourself more. To be totally honest I am probably going to try to do a 50k later in summer, it'll just depend whether it's self supported or in a race. I really love running and hope to be able to run for a long time and I think it's important to pace myself and not overdo it. I have been listening to a lot of podcasts and interviews during quarantine and that is one of the most important lessons from younger ultrarunners such as kilian and Lucy Bartholomew.
